title: forwardable defenseclaw substrate verify --json
description: Forwardable members of substrate-verify.schema.json (defenseclaw substrate verify --json). Project with allowlist-and-drop (forward/project.py). Everything but the checks' free-text messages passes: cluster and atespace names, the issuer digest, versions, counts, enums and times; no account, person or credential name appears in the document.

ok.description: False when any check failed; the command then exits 1.

policy_conflicts.description: The agents in policy_conflict per atespace (from 1.0.10). The policy_conflict check fails while one is there, and warns when they could not be counted.

cluster_name.description: k8s.cluster.name, as on every telemetry record.

issuer_sha256.description: SHA-256 of substrate.identity.issuer: a fleet compares these to find two clusters sharing an issuer (E13) without the URL.

issuer_default.description: The issuer has Substrate's default shape (https://idp.<namespace>.svc), which every cluster shares.

substrate_version.description: The Agent Substrate release (ate-api-server image tag). Absent when it could not be read.

edge_case.description: The plan edge case the check guards (E1 actor routes, E2 proxy takeover, E10 snapshots, E13 issuer).

policy_conflicts.description: The agents in policy_conflict (GAP-0398): after repeated foreign changes to an agent's network policy the controller keeps it on the DefenseClaw rule only (deny-only) until an administrator resets it. Read with the administrator's DefenseClaw sign-in (every person's agents); without one the count is unknown: read is false, reason says why, agents is null and atespaces is empty, never a 0.

read.description: Every person's agents were listed and counted.

agents.description: Every agent in policy_conflict; null (not forwarded) when not counted.

atespaces.description: Every launcher and managed atespace, and every other one with an agent in policy_conflict, sorted by name; empty when not counted.
